content.jointProblem: Can site-specific statistical and one-class models detect unusual Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP behaviour using only unlabelled operational traffic for training, while producing understandable alerts within ProtoSense's resource limits? The first experiment would compare interpretable baselines and an incremental detector on temporally held-out client captures and controlled bench scenarios, explicitly testing BACnet transfer, potentially contaminated training data, false-alert burden, detection delay, explanation usefulness and on-device overhead.

rationale.text: Kiss has directly relevant experience developing and operationally evaluating unsupervised SCADA detectors without labelled attack data.

sources.quote: The project developed threshold calibration procedures for detectors operating without labelled attack data
enabling validation under real traffic conditions.

rationale.text: Her Modbus research provides a concrete starting point for site-specific baselines using register-level timing, values and command sequences.

sources.quote: For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated using kernel density estimation

rationale.text: Her work addresses adaptation to operational changes, including an operator-acknowledged reset mechanism that could be investigated rather than adapting blindly to every anomaly.

sources.quote: Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed

rationale.text: She has studied threshold calibration using unlabelled operational data, directly relevant to the company's false-positive problem.

sources.quote: proposes a post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data.

rationale.text: Her embedded-gateway experiments provide relevant deployment experience, although their performance must be remeasured on ArmaturaSec hardware.

sources.quote: Experiments used three autoencoder architectures differing in depth (2, 4, 6 hidden layers) trained on Modbus/TCP and DNP3 captures.
A combined 8-bit quantised, 25%-pruned model achieved inference at 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target

rationale.text: Her preference for real-infrastructure deployment and access to an ICS testbed support an applied joint project with a controlled validation stage.

sources.quote: Kiss prefers applied collaborations that result in deployment on real infrastructure rather than purely synthetic experiments.
The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators

constraints.text: Training and operational threshold selection must not require confirmed client attack examples; the detector must learn a site-specific baseline rather than depend on supervised public-dataset training.

sources.quote: we have nothing labelled as malicious.
What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site

constraints.text: The scope must cover both Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP, with false-alert burden and plant-manager-readable explanations treated as acceptance requirements.

sources.quote: ProtoSense: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic
it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off.
we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

constraints.text: Inference must run on the company's embedded appliance without compromising packet-forwarding performance; actual hardware and latency budgets must be established before implementation.

sources.quote: Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build)
we have the hardware to run inference on-device
support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency.

constraints.text: Archive and firmware access must follow the company's NDA arrangements, and university testbed use requires a data-sharing agreement; existing collection consent must not be assumed to cover research sharing.

sources.quote: with access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA.
Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement.
we have collected several terabytes of captures from consenting clients over the past three years

constraints.text: The implementation and integration plan must fit one to two part-time company engineers rather than assume a dedicated development team.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project

risks: BACnet validation is not demonstrated in the supplied researcher material. Modbus/DNP3 results cannot establish BACnet performance; the first experiment must test BACnet-specific features and controlled scenarios separately.

The supposedly normal archives may contain undetected compromises. Baselines could normalise malicious behaviour, and unlabelled score distributions alone cannot establish a true operational false-positive rate.
Controlled attacks and prior testbeds may not represent client process diversity or stealthy attacks. Bench detection results would not validate real-world attack coverage.
Seasonality, maintenance and process reconfiguration may generate excessive alerts; automatic adaptation could also absorb persistent attacks unless update safeguards are tested.

Prior embedded measurements concern different processors and workloads. Actual appliance capacity, protocol-processing contention and the current status of the planned security-processor variant are unknown.
Plain-language explanations have not been validated with plant managers in the supplied evidence; technically interpretable features may still produce unhelpful alerts.
Researcher availability, project budget, delivery dates and ongoing maintenance ownership are unknown. Limited company engineering time could impede integration.
questions: What researcher and student time is available, and what funding, milestones and delivery schedule can both parties commit to?
Which appliance will host the pilot, is the planned security-processor variant available, and what CPU, RAM, storage, traffic-rate and latency limits apply?

Which sites and operating modes are represented in the archives, how much BACnet traffic is available, and are maintenance records, asset inventories and process-change logs available for interpretation?
Do client permissions cover university research access and controlled replay, and what NDA, data-sharing, retention and publication restrictions are required?
Can both protocols be reproduced safely on isolated benches, and who will approve and document controlled anomalies without injecting attacks into production?
What alert burden per site and detection delay are acceptable, who will adjudicate pilot alerts, and what plant-manager explanation would count as useful?
How should suspected training contamination and baseline updates be handled, and which changes require operator approval?
Who will own firmware integration, model updates, rollback and long-term support after the pilot?
